prompt.description: Instructions for what to extract from each conversation transcript (e.g. "Extract the candidate's salary expectations"). Automatically assessed and improved before creation unless skip_improvement=true.

value_type.description: Data type of the extracted value. Prefer constrained outputs so results can be filtered and grouped: boolean for yes/no; number for scores/ratings (e.g. 1-5); list for multiple items (not comma-separated text); single_line_text for categories — constrain the prompt to a fixed value set (e.g. 'Respond with exactly one of: None, Low, Moderate, High'), never free-form text with explanations. Use long_text only for genuinely open-ended answers.

field_id.description: Field ID of an existing AI field to update ('AI:<uuid>'); omit to create a new field. On update, changing the prompt, value_type, or name (for auto-prompted fields) CLEARS all existing results and triggers re-analysis on next query. System (prefab) fields cannot be updated.

skip_similarity_check.description: Create only. True skips the duplicate-field check and forces creation. Use when a previous call returned already_existed=true but the suggested field does not meet your needs. Default false.

skip_improvement.description: Create only. True skips the automatic prompt/value_type assessment and improvement, creating the field exactly as specified. Default false. Both what you submit and the improved version are compliance-checked; if the error says only the improved version was rejected, set this true to create your own wording as-is.

description.text:
<usecase>
Create a new AI field, or update an existing one (pass field_id).

AI fields are the primary tool for analyzing conversations at scale: each field defines a question answered independently for every conversation, so you can extract structured data from hundreds of conversations without reading transcripts. Use the field's results via search_conversations or group_conversations. Prefer this over bulk-fetching transcripts whenever 20+ conversations are involved.

IMPORTANT: Always confirm the field (name, prompt, value type) with the user before calling — fields analyze every conversation they are used against and results persist to the workspace. If the request is broad, suggest 2-3 focused fields (e.g. sentiment, objections, salary) rather than one catch-all.

DEDUPE: a create call may return an EXISTING matching field (already_existed=true, with match_quality and similarity_explanation) instead of creating one — ALWAYS check already_existed. If the match is not what you need, retry with skip_similarity_check=true.
</usecase>

<instructions>
Prompts are auto-assessed and improved before creation unless skip_improvement=true — focus on WHAT question to answer, not exact wording. Check list_fields(search_term=...) for existing AI and prefab fields before creating.
Results compute asynchronously: query the field via search_conversations or group_conversations; while ai_processing is present, retry every ~30s. Always apply tight filters — broad unfiltered queries are slow and may hit evaluation limits.
</instructions>

<response_format>
{"field_id" ("AI:<uuid>"), "name", "value_type",
 create: "already_existed", "match_quality"?, "similarity_explanation"?,
   "improved"?, "improvement_explanation"?,
 update: "updated"}
</response_format>

Filter value formats are data, not prose: list_fields returns a filter_formats map (operations + value_format per field type; a field's type key selects its entry). IMPORTANT: date filter values are a dict, not a bare date string. Example: {"field_id": "default:start_time", "operation": "after", "value": {"scope": "relative", "value": -2592000}}

report_id.description: UUID of an existing report to update. Omit to create a new report. On update, only the parameters you provide change.

field_ids.description: Field IDs (from list_fields) shown as the report's table columns.

sort_field.description: Field ID to sort conversation rows by (applied together with field_ids). Mutually exclusive with sort_metric, which sorts groups instead — never pass both.

sort_ascending.description: Sort direction for sort_field (default true = ascending).

metrics.description: Metrics computed per group on a grouped report. Each dict: metric_id (required, 'aggregation:...' or 'AI:<uuid>' from list_fields), function ('mean'|'median'|'sum'|'max'|'min'; default 'mean'), metric_arguments (optional dict — check required_arguments from list_fields). Defaults are applied when creating a grouped report without metrics.

sort_metric.description: How to sort groups on a grouped report: {metric_id, function ('mean'|'median'|'sum'|'max'|'min'), metric_arguments?} — same shape as metrics entries. Mutually exclusive with sort_field, which sorts conversation rows instead — never pass both.

sort_metric_ascending.description: Sort direction for sort_metric (default true = ascending).

only_show_recorded_conversations.description: True: the report covers only recorded conversations (creation default). False: also include unrecorded ones. Omit on update to leave unchanged.

expand_rows.description: Show grouped report rows expanded in the web-app UI.

min_group_conversation_count.description: Minimum conversations a group must have to appear in a grouped report.

description.text:
<usecase>
Save ONE clip of a conversation as a snippet and return links to it. The snippet appears on the conversation's snippets tab and gets its own share link. Call once per clip.

Take times from search_snippets previews (preferred), or from the '@M:SS-M:SS' transcript lines of search_conversations for a moment you found yourself.
</usecase>

<instructions>Create only the clips the user wants, usually the best 1-2. Never create snippets in bulk: don't slice whole conversations into clips or loop over many conversations to export, archive or summarize them. Use search_conversations to read conversations instead. Write a short title (max 7 words) and a one-sentence note on why the moment matters; omitted copy is generated but slower. share_scope defaults to anyone_in_org. Use anyone_with_link ONLY when the user explicitly asks for a public or external link; never infer it. Give the user share_link.url when present, otherwise snippets_tab_url (it lists every snippet on the conversation), and say whether the link is public.</instructions>

<response_format>
{"conversation_id", "snippet": {"snippet_id", "start_ms", "end_ms", "range", "title", "note"},
 "snippets_tab_url", "share_link": {"url", "scope"} | null}
</response_format>

<notes>Safe to retry: the same clip range on the same conversation returns your existing snippet instead of saving a duplicate. Clip video takes about a minute to render after creation. Workspace sharing settings can narrow or remove the share link; the message explains why.</notes>

description.text:
<usecase>
Enrich email addresses or phone numbers for one or more candidates. Starts an asynchronous contact lookup that SPENDS workspace enrichment credits.

IMPORTANT: Never call this tool until the user has received the required credit estimate and given a final explicit go-ahead.
</usecase>

<instructions>
REQUIRED CONFIRMATION BEFORE EVERY CALL:
1. Call get_enrichment_status with the candidate_ids immediately before proposing. Read credits.total_available, or on shared credits (credits is null) call get_platform_credits for the balance.
2. Estimate cost from the unique submitted candidate IDs not in free_candidate_ids: 3 credits per candidate for email, 10 for phone. Candidates in free_candidate_ids cost nothing.
3. Tell the user: enrichment type, candidate count, estimated cost, available credits, and projected remainder. Explain the final charge is per net-new contact found, so it can be lower (skips, nothing found) or higher (multiple contacts per candidate).
4. Wait for an explicit yes AFTER showing these figures — a general or earlier approval is not sufficient.
If the estimate exceeds the balance, do not call; report the shortfall.
Candidates must belong to the workspace and have a stored LinkedIn URL. Candidates whose latest same-type enrichment succeeded or is in progress are skipped (a failed attempt stays eligible), so repeating the request advances through large lists without re-enriching.
The lookup completes asynchronously — check progress with get_enrichment_status (include_enrichment_attempts=true). enrichment_started=false means nothing was needed or possible.
</instructions>

<response_format>{"requested_candidate_count", "processed_candidate_count", "not_found_candidate_count", "existing_enrichment_candidate_count", "truncated_candidate_count", "enrichment_type", "enrichment_ids", "enrichment_started"}</response_format>

candidates.description:
1-10 candidate lookups. Each is a dict with at least one identifier key — these exact keys and no others:
- candidate_id: Metaview candidate UUID (as returned by the application review, screening, and sourcing candidate tools).
- linkedin_url: LinkedIn profile URL ("https://www.linkedin.com/in/john-doe") or bare shorthand ("john-doe").
- email: candidate email address.
- phone_number: candidate phone number.
- participant_id: Metaview participant ID (e.g. from the default:candidate field in conversation data).
Optional scoped-access keys (each requires candidate_id and an accessible entity whose roster includes the candidate):
- application_review_id: Application Review UUID authorizing ATS access.
- screen_id: screen UUID authorizing ATS access.

description.text:
<usecase>
Look up people/candidates and get, per candidate: profile (professional background — experience, education, skills, location; resolved from a LinkedIn URL, given or found in ATS data) and ats (scorecards, applications with status and stage, interviewer feedback, files such as resumes with download URLs). Metaview mirrors the user's ATS records — mirrors sync every ~30 minutes, so data may lag the ATS slightly.

Use this for scorecard results, application status or stage, resumes, profiles, and interviewer feedback.

ATS data access requires one of: Metaview admin; ATS admin; the candidate appeared in a conversation you can access; or a lookup carries an accessible application_review_id/screen_id whose roster includes the candidate. Review-/screen-scoped access returns applications and files but withholds scorecards and global ATS feedback; it stays available during reranks and is review-wide for multi-job reviews. Candidates you can't access are reported as not found.
</usecase>

<instructions>Provide multiple identifiers per lookup when known for better matching. Per-candidate failures come back as an error entry for that lookup, not a tool error.</instructions>

<response_format>
{"candidates": [{"lookup",
  "profile"?: {"name", "linkedin_url", "location", ...},
  "ats"?: {"name", "applications": [{"job_title", "status", "stage"}],
    "scorecards": [{"question", "answer_or_score"}], "feedback",
    "files": [{"file_name", "download_url"}]},
  "error"?, "message"?}]}
</response_format>

<examples>fetch_candidates(candidates=[{"email": "john@example.com"}, {"candidate_id": "c1a2b3d4-...", "screen_id": "550e8400-..."}])</examples>

chart_inputs.description: Chart specifications, each a dict with: metric_id (str, required) — 'aggregation:...' or 'AI:<uuid>' from list_fields. function (str) — one of Average, Median, Count, Sum, Max, Min, Cumulative, Rolling Average; must be in the metric's chart_functions. interval (str) — one of day, week, month, quarter. function and interval MUST be provided together (aggregate chart) or both omitted (scatter chart; the metric must have 'scatter' in chart_types). metric_arguments (dict, optional) — check required_arguments from list_fields. For contact-scoped metrics (question_count, talk_time, minutes_late) you MUST pass {"scope": "internal"} or {"scope": "external"}. "internal" = interviewers/hiring team, "external" = non-team participants (candidates, clients, etc.). function_arguments (dict, optional) — for Rolling Average pass {"windowIntervalCount": <int>}.

report_id.description: UUID of a saved report (from search_reports) to use as the base filter set. Filters passed alongside apply on top.

filters.description: Filter objects, each {field_id, operation, value}, scoping which conversations are charted. Filter value formats are data, not prose: list_fields returns a filter_formats map (operations + value_format per field type; a field's type key selects its entry). IMPORTANT: date filter values are a dict, not a bare date string. Example: {"field_id": "default:start_time", "operation": "after", "value": {"scope": "relative", "value": -2592000}}

only_show_recorded_conversations.description: True (default): chart only recorded conversations. False: also include unrecorded ones (calls that were not captured, or upcoming).

group.description: Field ID (e.g. 'OSPT:<uuid>', 'default:interviewer') to scope the chart to conversations that have a value for this field. This is a filter, NOT a breakdown — it does not split the chart per group member; for per-group metrics use group_conversations. Must be a field ID, never a metric ('aggregation:...') ID.

min_count.description: Minimum conversations per group when group is set (default 0).

timezone_offset_minutes.description: Timezone offset in minutes for date bucketing (default 0 = UTC). Aggregate charts only.

rationale.description: Always provide a brief explanation of why you are calling this tool

description.text:
<usecase>
Get chart data: aggregate time-series (line/bar) or scatter plots.

Each chart_input is processed independently and its mode is determined by the keys present — include BOTH function and interval for an aggregate (time-bucketed) chart; omit BOTH for a values (scatter) chart with one point per conversation.

IMPORTANT: only metrics with "scatter" in their chart_types (from list_fields) support scatter plots; e.g. Conversation Count is aggregate-only.

For breakdowns by a field use group_conversations; for individual conversation rows use search_conversations.
</usecase>

<instructions>Discover metric IDs and their supported chart_types and chart_functions with list_fields; look up filter values with list_field_values.</instructions>

<response_format>
{"charts": [{"metric_id", "function"?, "interval"?, "error"?,
   "data": [aggregate: {"start_date", "value", "values": [{"label", "value"}]}
            | scatter: {"conversation_id", "date_time", "value", "label"}]}],
 "ai_processing"?: {"AI:<uuid>": {"pending_count", "total_count"}}}
</response_format>

<notes>Note: AI field values are computed asynchronously — if "ai_processing" is present in the response, poll by retrying the same call every ~30 seconds. Always apply tight filters before using AI fields. See search_conversations for the full AI field evaluation guidance.</notes>

person_id.description: Filter usage and attempts to this person (admin only). Non-admins always see only their own data regardless of this parameter.

month.description: Month to report on as YYYY-MM (e.g. "2026-01"). Scopes usage, usage_by_user, and enrichment_attempts to that calendar month; omit for the current month to date. Does NOT affect 'credits', which is always the live balance. Usage is null on shared credits.

include_usage_by_user.description: True: include the per-user usage breakdown (admin only). Default false.

include_enrichment_attempts.description: True: append the list of individual enrichment attempts. Default false.

enrichment_type.description: Filter attempts by type (email or phone). Only used when include_enrichment_attempts=true.

limit.description: Attempts per page (default 50; values above 100 are clamped to 100).

candidate_ids.description: Candidates you are about to enrich. Returns free_candidate_ids: those that enrich at no cost, because Metaview sourced them, the workspace is on shared credits and today's free enrichment limit still covers them. When the limit runs short, earlier candidate_ids take priority.

rationale.description: Always provide a brief explanation of why you are calling this tool

description.text:
<usecase>
Get the workspace's contact-enrichment credit status and usage breakdown, optionally with a per-user breakdown (include_usage_by_user=true) and individual enrichment attempts (include_enrichment_attempts=true).

KEY DISTINCTION: 'credits' is the LIVE balance right now and ignores the month parameter; 'usage', 'usage_by_user', and 'enrichment_attempts' are scoped to the requested month (or the current month to date when month is omitted).
</usecase>

<instructions>Without shared credits, workspaces receive a base allowance of 500 credits per month; top-up purchases add to it. On shared credits, enrichment draws on the workspace's shared credits, so 'credits', 'top_ups', 'usage', 'usage_by_user' and each attempt's 'credits_consumed' are null: call get_platform_credits for usage and remaining credits. Non-admins always see only their own usage and attempts. Pass candidate_ids before proposing an enrichment: free_candidate_ids lists those that cost no credits.</instructions>

<response_format>
{"credits": {"monthly_limit", "monthly_used", "monthly_remaining",
   "top_up_credits_available", "total_available", "warning_threshold_reached"}
   | null (live balance, month-independent; null on shared credits),
 "usage": {"email": {"enrichments_count", "credits_used"},
   "phone": {...}, "total_credits_used"} | null (month-scoped; null on shared credits),
 "period_start", "period_end"?,
 "top_ups": [{"credits_purchased", "credits_used", "credits_remaining", "expires_at"}] | null,
 "usage_by_user"? [{...}], "workspace_total_credits_used"?,
 "enrichment_attempts"? [{...}], "enrichment_attempts_total_count"?,
 "enrichment_attempts_has_more"?, "free_candidate_ids"? [str] (when candidate_ids is passed)}
</response_format>

Use send_job_post_message to respond and list_job_post_threads for suggestions. Returns the newest run per visible check (up to 100), with verdict, completion and outdated flags. For current failures, count posts with a failed, non-outdated run. If check_runs_truncated is true and no current failure is returned, the post's failure status is unknown.</instructions>

<usecase>
Record a REJECT or PROGRESS decision on one or more admitted candidates in an Application Review, optionally with free-text feedback.

IMPORTANT: this is a live decision, not a draft. Decisions sync to the customer's connected ATS — a REJECT can move the candidate's ATS stage and send a rejection email; a PROGRESS can advance their ATS stage. These effects are visible to the hiring team and, for rejection emails, to the candidate. Reviews with applicant_source UPLOAD have no ATS: their decisions are saved in Metaview only. Only call this tool with decisions the user has confirmed.

description.text:
<usecase>
Group conversations by a field and compute per-group counts and metrics. Prefer this tool for 'how many', breakdowns, distributions, rankings, and 'by X' questions; time-series trends → get_chart_data; individual rows → search_conversations.

POWERFUL PATTERN for finding trends across many conversations:
1. Create an AI field (create_ai_field) extracting the data point of interest.
2. Group by that AI field to see its value distribution, or group by another field (e.g. interviewer) with the AI field as a metric.
This avoids reading raw transcripts and works at any scale.
</usecase>

<instructions>Find groupable field IDs (groupable=true) and metric IDs with list_fields; look up filter values with list_field_values.</instructions>

<response_format>
{"groups": [{"label", "value", "conversation_count",
   "metric_values"?: {"<metric_id>:<function>": 156.0}}],
 "total_groups", "total_conversation_count", "has_more",
 "ai_processing"?: {"AI:<uuid>": {"pending_count", "total_count"}}}
</response_format>

<notes>
Note: AI field values are computed asynchronously — if "ai_processing" is present in the response, poll by retrying the same call every ~30 seconds. Always apply tight filters before using AI fields. See search_conversations for the full AI field evaluation guidance.

IMPORTANT: while ai_processing is present, counts are incomplete — grouping by an AI field can make the groups' conversation_count sum to LESS than total_conversation_count, and filtering by an AI field excludes not-yet-evaluated conversations (lowering total_conversation_count). Wait for pending_count to reach 0 before treating counts as complete.
</notes>

This is the feedback half of ICP refinement: after an ICP update reranks the review, use this to verify the bar moved the way you intended.

During routine incremental evaluation of new applicants the stable ACTIVE ranking is served, with pending_evaluation_count noting how many are not yet scored.
The response echoes active_version — the ACTIVE ICP display version the returned fit bands were computed against (null when the review has no active ranking yet).

<usecase>
List the Application Reviews you can access, with run state, ICP version and roster counts.

Find a review to inspect or refine here, then get_application_review_details for its ICP and version history, or list_application_review_candidates for the ranked applicants.
</usecase>

Access: ATS hiring-team membership, admin, explicit share, or all-member access.

</instructions>

<data_model>
- A REVIEW ranks a job's inbound applicants (from the ATS, or uploaded CVs when applicant_source is UPLOAD) against an ICP (Ideal Candidate Profile).
- ICP versions: DRAFT (proposed, not applied) -> RANKING (approved, full rerank in flight) -> ACTIVE (live) -> ARCHIVED. Version numbers are web-app display numbers (approved versions 1..N, oldest first); a pending DRAFT is unnumbered.
- An ICP edit triggers a FULL RERANK of every admitted candidate (free but heavyweight); a RESTORE mints a NEW version from an ARCHIVED one, reusing prior evaluations (fast).
- ADMISSION: ADMITTED (ranked roster; charged at admission) or PENDING (a count, never rows).
- FIT: coarse band only (great/good/okay/no_evidence/poor); numeric scores and rank positions never exposed. FRAUD RISK (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH) is advisory, full detail only.
- DECISION: PROGRESSED / REJECTED / null (undecided); syncs to the ATS (stage moves, rejection emails), except on UPLOAD reviews (saved in Metaview only).
</data_model>

description.text:
<usecase>
Get the possible values of one field — e.g. all departments, interviewer names, or job titles. Essential for looking up the person/participant IDs that PERSON- and PARTICIPANT-type filters require.

Prefer search_term when looking for a specific value; results can also be scoped to a report or filter set so only values appearing in matching conversations are returned.
</usecase>

<instructions>
Contact lookup — the same person can have MULTIPLE contact records. To avoid duplicates: interviewers/employees → field_id='default:interviewer'; candidates → 'default:candidate'; unknown role → 'default:contact' (may return several records per person; check is_internal).
search_term supports substring matching and regex (auto-detected when the term contains regex characters). Prefer first and last name together; disambiguate before proceeding when several results return.
Filter value formats are data, not prose: list_fields returns a filter_formats map (operations + value_format per field type; a field's type key selects its entry). IMPORTANT: date filter values are a dict, not a bare date string. Example: {"field_id": "default:start_time", "operation": "after", "value": {"scope": "relative", "value": -2592000}}
</instructions>

<response_format>
{"field_id", "values": [{"value" (string, or int person ID, or UUID contact ID),
   "label", "person"? ({first_name, last_name, email, is_internal? — participant
   fields only})}],
 "has_more"}
</response_format>

description.text:
<usecase>
Discover the fields and metrics for reports queries — call this first for analytics tasks.

Returns FIELDS (IDs like 'default:start_time', 'OSPT:<uuid>', 'AI:<uuid>') for filters, group_by, columns, chart group; and METRICS ('aggregation:...') ONLY for metric_id in group_conversations and chart_inputs in get_chart_data. Never mix the ID kinds.

The response's filter_formats map (operations + value format per field type) is the filter grammar for search_conversations, group_conversations, get_chart_data, create_report.
</usecase>

<instructions>
Prefer search_term over fetching all. Ranked: exact and substring/regex first, then closest fuzzy matches (match='fuzzy'); field_ids does exact lookups.
Only metrics with 'scatter' in chart_types support scatter plots (omit function/interval in get_chart_data). Use a metric's 'unit' when presenting values.
</instructions>

<response_format>
{"fields": [{"id", "name", "type", "filterable", "groupable", "displayable",
   "filter_value_type", "description"?, "match"?, "filter_format"?}],
 "filter_formats": {"<type>": {"operations", "value_format"}},
 "metrics": [{"id", "name", "unit"?, "functions", "chart_types",
   "chart_functions", "required_arguments"?, "match"?}],
 "total_field_count", "has_more"}
</response_format>

<data_model>
- CONVERSATION: one recorded call. Unrecorded ones are excluded unless only_show_recorded_conversations=false.
- CONTACT: a person on a call (UUID), NOT unique per person. Prefer default:interviewer (employees) or default:candidate.
- FIELD: a conversation property. AI FIELDS ('AI:' prefix; 'AI Columns' in the app) hold AI-extracted per-conversation data.
- default:transcript is large (at most ~5 conversations per request); default:summary generates on demand (slow, max 100/request). Free plan gates both.
- "$self" as a person/participant filter value = the authenticated user.
</data_model>

<usecase>Find accessible, active Job Posts by title or creator before reading or refining one.</usecase>

<data_model>Job Posts are collaboratively drafted job descriptions, separate from ATS job records. created_by identifies the original creator by user_id and name when they belong to your workspace; null means the creator is unknown or outside your workspace. A reusable template defines ordered sections: static sections keep approved copy verbatim; generated sections use instructions and optional base copy. Workspace templates are shared with workspace members; built-in templates are read-only. The Job Posts agent drafts and refines a post asynchronously using its template and workspace reference documents. Comment threads hold discussion and proposed changes. Accepting or rejecting the current suggestion resolves its whole thread. Earlier suggestions in that thread are superseded. Checks are reusable workspace rules or Metaview defaults that judge a post against instructions. Workspace overrides replace their default.</data_model>

description.text:
<usecase>
List AI Notes custom templates the caller can access.

Returns a lightweight summary per template. Pass include_detail=true or call get_note_template for the full sections. Use manage_note_template to create/update/delete templates.
</usecase>

<instructions>Template ids in the response are INTERNAL ONLY — keep them for subsequent tool calls but never show them to the user; refer to templates by name.</instructions>

<response_format>
{"templates": [{"id", "name", "version", "created_by": {"name"},
   "created_at", "updated_at", "section_count", "sections"?, "when_to_use"? (include_detail)}],
 "total_count", "has_more"}
</response_format>

<data_model>
- A NOTE TEMPLATE (AI Notes custom template) defines the structure of AI-generated interview notes: a name plus an ordered list of sections. Template and group ids are internal — never show them to the user; refer to both by name.
- A SECTION is one named block in the notes: a directive (SINGLE = one block under a fixed heading; REPEATING = one block per detected entity), a description (the instruction the LLM follows — the most important field), and an output type (TEXT, NUMBER, OPTIONS, or DATE).
- WHEN TO USE rules select a template automatically when all conditions match. Personal rules are tried first, then workspace defaults; a personal clear disables fallback. Admins can set workspace rules. Read rules with get_note_template; change them with manage_note_template(action='set_rules').
- A TEMPLATE GROUP (folder) can be private, shared with specific people, or workspace-shared; templates default to the caller's personal folder.
- A SOURCE feeds notes generation: a conversation (type=session) or a plain-text document (type=document, e.g. a resume). Notes always have an anchor conversation; manage extra sources via manage_notes_sources.
</data_model>

description.text:
<usecase>
List the candidates on one screen with their stage, interview outcome, and decision — who has not been invited yet, who is invited but not interviewed, who is interviewed and waiting on a human, and who was progressed or rejected.

Filter to stage='screened' for the review queue, then get_screen_interview to read the scorecard behind a candidate's fit. For a candidate's full profile, resume, or ATS application detail, call fetch_candidates with the candidate_id and this screen_id — this tool owns only what the screen knows.
</usecase>

<instructions>
Order is best-fit first (great, good, okay, no_evidence, poor). Unscored candidates rank in the no_evidence band; tell them apart by overall_fit, which reads "no_evidence" for a scored candidate and null for an unscored one.
Every field describes the candidate's most recent interview. overall_fit and bluf are null until it has been scored (not interviewed, still IN_PROGRESS / EVALUATING, or sent back for re-scoring by a plan update) — treat rank as a hint when fit is missing.
authenticity (medium only) is advisory and prompts human review, never an automatic decision; active human corrections replace the original risk and reasoning.
opted_out candidates count as SCREENED so they surface in the review queue, but never interviewed and carry no fit.
</instructions>

<response_format>
Minimal (default):
{"screen_id", "candidates": [{"candidate_id", "name", "stage", "overall_fit", "decision", "opted_out", "admitted_at"}], "total_count", "has_more"}
Medium adds per candidate:
{"bluf", "interview_status", "interview_completed_at", "decided_at", "decision_feedback", "authenticity": {"ai_use": {"risk", "reasoning"}, "misrepresentation"}}
</response_format>

<data_model>See list_screens for the Screening data model.</data_model>

description.text:
<usecase>
List the Screening screens you can access, with ATS job posts, active plan version, pending-changes flag, and roster counts by stage.

Use this to find a screen, then get_screen_details for its interview plan and version history, or list_screen_candidates for its candidates.
</usecase>

<instructions>
Access: ATS hiring-team membership, admin, or explicit share.
candidates.screened is the queue awaiting a human decision. has_pending_changes: web-app edits not in use until Update screen. No active_version = no candidates invited yet.
</instructions>

<response_format>{"screens": [{"id", "job_title", "location", "ats_job_post_ids", "active_version"?: {"version", "lifecycle_state", "is_draft", "changelog", "created_at", "activated_at", "activated_by"}, "has_pending_changes", "candidates": {"pending", "pre_screen", "screened", "progressed", "rejected"}, "created_at", "updated_at"}], "total_count", "has_more"}</response_format>

<data_model>
- SCREEN: the per-job record (plan, roster, results), optionally linked to ATS job posts. Each candidate takes an AI interview scored against the plan.
- PLAN: question sections + role/company context. Once candidates are invited, the ACTIVE version is what interviews run against and web-app edits stay pending until Update screen; scoring changes applied then re-score undecided interviews.
- STAGE (derived): PENDING -> PRE_SCREEN (admitted + invited; spends credits) -> SCREENED (interviewed, or opted out) -> PROGRESSED / REJECTED (human, terminal; syncs to the ATS as stage moves and rejections where wired).
- FIT: band only (great/good/okay/no_evidence/poor), no numeric scores. AUTHENTICITY (ai_use, misrepresentation: LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH) is advisory.
- OUTREACH: invitation email + schedule; deadlines snapshot at admission.
- Writes: update_screen_plan and update_screen_outreach only; all else read-only.
</data_model>

description.text:
<usecase>
List sequences the current user can access, or fetch one sequence's full detail (pass sequence_id).

Admins see all workspace sequences; non-admins see sequences they created plus any sending from their mailbox. Archived sequences are excluded. Summary rows include per-sequence stats for comparison without further calls.
Related: list_sequence_candidates for enrolled candidates, manage_sequence to create/edit, list_mailboxes for sendable mailboxes.
</usecase>

<instructions>Pass sequence_id or include_detail=true to get full step configuration. Test sends and email previews are only available in the Metaview web app.</instructions>

<response_format>
{"sequences": [{"id", "name", "description", "is_enabled", "is_valid",
   "is_modifiable", "created_by": {"name"}, "created_at", "updated_at",
   "step_count", "stats": {"total_candidates", "total_active",
     "total_completed", "total_paused", "total_sent", "total_replies",
     "total_bounced", "total_interested"},
   "steps"? (with include_detail)}],
 "total_count", "has_more"}
</response_format>

<data_model>
- A SEQUENCE is an outreach campaign of ordered steps. Sequences can be enabled/disabled, lock (non-modifiable) once the first email is sent, and only their creator can edit them.
- A STEP is one action in a sequence (channel types: EMAIL, LINKEDIN_CONNECTION, LINKEDIN_INMAIL, LINKEDIN_MESSAGE, SMS, PHONE, WHATSAPP) with content templates and a schedule; it executes automatically or manually.
- A CANDIDATE SEQUENCE is one candidate's enrollment in a sequence: per-step delivery status, can be paused/resumed/cancelled, supports per-candidate template and schedule overrides.
- A MAILBOX is an email account that can send sequence emails; its id is the from_mailbox_id for EMAIL steps. A SEND-ON-BEHALF PERMISSION lets one person send as another (per-person or workspace-wide).
</data_model>

action.description: The operation to perform. cancel: stop further sends but keep the candidate visible. remove: delete (archive) the enrollment entirely. update: override one step's subject/body/schedule for this candidate.

template_override.description: update only. Custom body for this candidate's step; supports {{variable_name}} placeholders filled per-candidate by AI before sending. Mutually exclusive with clear_template_override (if both are set, the clear wins).

clear_subject_override.description: update only. True reverts the subject to the template default. Mutually exclusive with subject_override.

clear_template_override.description: update only. True reverts the body to the template default. Mutually exclusive with template_override.

Schedule override object, one of: {"schedule_type": "instant"}; {"schedule_type": "next_business_day", "time_of_day": "HH:MM" or "HH:MM:SS"}; {"schedule_type": "later", "delay_seconds": N}. specific_time is NOT supported. Mutually exclusive with clear_schedule_override (if both are set, the clear wins).

context_source_type.description: add only. Must be 'search' and requires context_source_id. Leave BOTH context_source_type and context_source_id null when the source is unknown — do NOT guess or fabricate a value.

description.text:

action.description: The operation to perform: create, update, delete, or set_rules.

template_id.description: Template UUID. Required when action=update, delete, or set_rules. INTERNAL ONLY — never surface this id to the user; refer to templates by name.

name.description: Template name. Required when action=create; optional for update (renames).

sections.description:
Ordered list of section objects (list order = display order; max 100). Required when action=create; optional for update. FULL REPLACE on update: the list replaces ALL existing sections — omitted sections are removed. Include a section's existing id to update it in place; omit id for new sections.
Section shape (every field required):
  directive: 'SINGLE' (one block under a fixed heading) | 'REPEATING' (one block per detected entity — prefer this whenever the intent is 'one block per X', instead of several near-identical SINGLE sections)
  heading: str — required when directive='SINGLE'
  repeating_entity: str — required when directive='REPEATING' (e.g. 'Question', 'Topic', 'Role', 'Project')
  description: str — THE most important field: a PROMPT run on every transcript, not a note to a human. Cover (a) SCOPE — what to include and leave out — and (b) OUTPUT FORMAT — length caps, markdown patterns, label conventions (e.g. '3 bullets max, each **Label:** one sentence, under 120 words'). REPEATING descriptions run once per detected entity.
  output: dict, one of:
    {'type': 'TEXT', 'text_format': 'PARAGRAPH'|'BULLET_POINT', 'detail': 'low'|'medium'|'high'} — use TEXT for anything that isn't a hard classification; carry structure via markdown in the description.
    {'type': 'NUMBER', 'currency': str} — '' for a plain number, else 'USD', 'EUR', ...
    {'type': 'OPTIONS', 'options_type': 'SINGLE'|'MULTIPLE', 'options': [str, ...]} — the description MUST give per-option selection criteria (exactly when to pick each value and when NOT to); for booleans use options=['true', 'false'] with options_type='SINGLE'.
    {'type': 'DATE', 'date_format': str, e.g. 'yyyy/mm/dd'|'mm/dd/yyyy'|'dd/mm/yyyy'}

group_name.description: update only. Move the template into a named accessible folder; pass '' or 'personal' for the personal folder. Resolve folder names via list_note_template_groups first. Omit to leave the template where it is.

filters.description: Required for set_rules only. Full replacement of When to Use conditions, combined with AND. Pass [] to disable automatic selection for the chosen scope. Each object has field_id, operation, and value. Discover field IDs/operations with list_fields and values with list_field_values. Filter value formats are data, not prose: list_fields returns a filter_formats map (operations + value_format per field type; a field's type key selects its entry). IMPORTANT: date filter values are a dict, not a bare date string. Example: {"field_id": "default:start_time", "operation": "after", "value": {"scope": "relative", "value": -2592000}}

apply_to_workspace.description: set_rules only. False (default): personal rules. True: admin-only workspace rules, replacing everyone's personal copies; $self is not allowed. An admin saving personal rules also disables workspace rules for this template. Rules affect future automatic selection; existing notes are not regenerated.

<instructions>Design guidance: write every section description like a production LLM prompt — explicit scope plus an output-format contract (descriptions under ~200 characters produce vague notes). Bias toward one REPEATING section over several near-identical SINGLE sections. Split sections when outputs have different shapes or the user iterates on them independently. Use OPTIONS sparingly: 2-5 well-defined values with per-option criteria; a 6+ value enum is usually a classification a TEXT section handles better.</instructions>

Create / update: {"template": {template detail without rules}}
set_rules: {"template": {template detail, "when_to_use"}}
Delete: {"deleted": true, "template_id"}

action.description: The operation to perform: create, update, duplicate, or delete.

sequence_id.description: Sequence UUID. Required when action=update, duplicate, or delete.

name.description: Sequence name. Required when action=create; optional for update (renames).

description.description: Sequence description. Optional for create and update.

set_enabled.description: Enable or disable the sequence. Optional for create and update.

unsendable_step_behavior.description: What the sequence's AUTOMATIC steps do when they can't reach the candidate (no email, phone number or LinkedIn profile for the step's channel, WhatsApp rejects the number, or the email bounces): PAUSE_SEQUENCE pauses the candidate's sequence until someone fixes it; SKIP_STEP skips that step and the sequence carries on. Manual steps always pause. Optional for create and update.

steps.description:
FULL REPLACE (update action only): this list replaces the sequence's current steps — steps not in the list are DELETED. Each step's schedule is required (schedule_type values: instant, later, next_business_day; specific_time is rejected). time_of_day accepts 'HH:MM' or 'HH:MM:SS'.
    steps: Optional for update. A JSON list of step objects to replace the current steps.
        Steps not in the list are deleted. Order in the list determines step order.
        Each step object has:
            channel_type: str (REQUIRED — one of: EMAIL, LINKEDIN_CONNECTION, LINKEDIN_INMAIL, LINKEDIN_MESSAGE, SMS, PHONE, WHATSAPP)
            sequence_step_id: str | null (include the existing step ID to update it;
                omit or set null for new steps — an ID will be generated automatically)
            template: str | null (message body; supports {{variable_name}} placeholders
                that are filled in per-candidate by an AI call before sending)
            description: str | null
            schedule: dict | null (e.g. {"schedule_type": "instant"}, {"schedule_type": "later", "delay_seconds": 86400}, {"schedule_type": "next_business_day", "time_of_day": "09:00:00"}.
                Setting a specific time is NOT supported.
            step_execution_type: str | null (AUTOMATIC or MANUAL)
            execution_timeout_seconds: int | null (only for MANUAL steps)

        EMAIL step fields:
            step_type: REQUIRED (NEW_THREAD or REPLY)
            bcc: optional (list of email addresses)
            cc: optional (list of email addresses)
            from_mailbox_id: optional (mailbox UUID — use list_mailboxes to get available mailboxes; the sequence cannot be enabled until every EMAIL step has one)
            step_execution_type: AUTOMATIC, MANUAL (default: AUTOMATIC)
            NOT used: from_whatsapp_account_id, linkedin_subject
            step_type values: NEW_THREAD or REPLY
            subject: str | null (REQUIRED for NEW_THREAD; forbidden for REPLY. Supports {{variable_name}} placeholders)

        LINKEDIN_CONNECTION step fields:
            step_execution_type: MANUAL (default: MANUAL)
            NOT used: bcc, cc, from_mailbox_id, from_whatsapp_account_id, linkedin_subject, step_type
            Connection request with optional note; recommended maximum 275 characters including resolved placeholders (stored in template field)

        LINKEDIN_INMAIL step fields:
            linkedin_subject: REQUIRED (str — required subject line for the InMail)
            step_execution_type: MANUAL (default: MANUAL)
            NOT used: bcc, cc, from_mailbox_id, from_whatsapp_account_id, step_type
            InMail to non-connections. Requires subject + body. Uses Premium LinkedIn credits.

        LINKEDIN_MESSAGE step fields:
            linkedin_subject: optional (str | null — subject line for the LinkedIn message)
            step_execution_type: MANUAL (default: MANUAL)
            NOT used: bcc, cc, from_mailbox_id, from_whatsapp_account_id, step_type
            subject shorthand: setting 'subject' auto-maps to linkedin_subject

        SMS step fields:
            step_execution_type: MANUAL (default: MANUAL)
            NOT used: bcc, cc, from_mailbox_id, from_whatsapp_account_id, linkedin_subject, step_type

        PHONE step fields:
            step_execution_type: MANUAL (default: MANUAL)
            NOT used: bcc, cc, from_mailbox_id, from_whatsapp_account_id, linkedin_subject, step_type

        WHATSAPP step fields:
            from_whatsapp_account_id: optional (ignored; the connected sender is selected automatically)
            step_execution_type: AUTOMATIC, MANUAL (default: AUTOMATIC)
            NOT used: bcc, cc, from_mailbox_id, linkedin_subject, step_type
            Automatic steps use the step creator's connected WhatsApp account.

description.text:
<usecase>
Restore a previous Application Review ICP version: the restored content becomes a new latest version, is approved on the spot, and a rerank starts against it.

IMPORTANT: this applies immediately — no separate confirmation or approval step. It supersedes any pending, unapplied ICP draft, exactly as restoring in the web app does. The rerank after a restore is typically fast: prior evaluations against the restored content are reused, so only candidates that version never saw are re-evaluated.

A restore is itself reversible — the replaced version stays in version_history, so you can restore back to it.
</usecase>

<instructions>
Always call get_application_review_details first and pick the target from version_history; read a candidate version's full ICP text with icp_version=N before restoring it. Only a previous (superseded) version can be restored — the currently active version and a version mid-ranking are rejected.
Some reviews only allow ICP management in the Metaview web app; a restore against one is rejected. If a rerank is already running, the restore is rejected — poll for it to finish, then retry. The review can also reject the restored version on its content; the error says why and what to do.
</instructions>

<response_format>{"application_review_id", "restored_version", "status": "approved_and_ranking", "next"}</response_format>

description.text:
<usecase>
Search conversations with filters; return one row per conversation with requested fields.

Choose the right tool: 'how many' questions and breakdowns by attribute → group_conversations; time-series trends → get_chart_data. Use this tool only when you need individual conversation rows.

Scale strategy: 1-5 matching conversations, fields=['default:transcript']; 5-20, fields=['default:summary']; 20+, do NOT bulk-fetch transcripts or summaries — create an AI field (create_ai_field) and aggregate it here or in group_conversations. Unsure? Query default fields first and check total_count.
</usecase>

<instructions>
Get field IDs, operations, and filter_formats from list_fields; valid filter values from list_field_values.
A 1-hour transcript is ~10-15k tokens — keep limit low; prefer AI fields. Transcript lines are 'Name (Role) @M:SS-M:SS: text'; deep-link a moment with ?t=<seconds> on the conversation URL.
Summaries generate on the fly (slow, max 100/request); narrow filters first. When has_transcript is false, url is null: explain that no captured transcript is available instead of constructing a notes link.
</instructions>

{"field_definitions": [{"field_id", "name", "type"}],
 "conversations": [{"id", "url", "has_transcript", "fields": {"<field_id>": [{"value", "label",
   "details"? (entity fields: name, emails, phone_numbers)}]}}],
 "total_count", "has_more", "ai_processing"?: {"AI:<uuid>": {"pending_count", "total_count"}}}
</response_format>

<notes>While ai_processing is present, retry the same call every ~30s. Requesting an AI field evaluates all matching conversations; apply tight filters first. Results are cached.</notes>

description.text:
<usecase>
Start a sourcing or research search, or follow up to refine requirements, answer agent questions, or add context.

Source mode finds candidates; research mode answers market/talent questions with analysis and reports.

Do NOT message the agent with questions answerable from existing data — it works asynchronously. For a search's ICP, calibration, feedback, or status use get_search_details; for surfaced candidates use list_sourcing_candidates; for cross-search metrics use get_sourcing_analytics. Only message the agent when it must DO something (search, refine, calibrate, research).

One search per role or brief. To cover several target companies, segments or locations, list them all in ONE brief, or add them to an existing search by calling this tool with its search_id — NEVER create one search per company/segment/location, and NEVER create searches in parallel. Before creating, check list_sourcing_searches for an existing search for the role in the same mode (a research search never sources candidates) and follow up on it instead.
</usecase>

<instructions>A new search returns its ID — save it for follow-ups. The agent works asynchronously. For candidate searches, first matches are typically found within a minute; poll get_sourcing_messages until the phase leaves 'busy'. Discover connected data sources with list_connectors. Setting connectors updates this search's selection before the message is sent.</instructions>

description.text:

description.text:
<usecase>
Replace an Application Review's ideal candidate profile (ICP) and immediately rerank every admitted candidate against the new profile.

IMPORTANT: this is not a draft or a suggestion. The ICP text is written as a user edit, approved on the spot, and triggers a full rerank — no separate confirmation or approval step. Only call it with complete, final ICP text. It supersedes any pending, unapplied ICP draft, exactly as approving an edit in the web app does. The edit is reversible — restore a prior version with restore_application_review_icp.

Always call get_application_review_details first: read the current ICP, compose the full revised profile, and pass the active_icp version number as base_version so a concurrent edit isn't silently clobbered.
</usecase>

<instructions>
Reranks consume no credits but are heavyweight on large reviews. After calling, poll get_application_review_details with detail_level='concise' — the version moves RANKING then ACTIVE. Candidate listings are unavailable until it completes, and a further ICP update is rejected while the rerank is in flight.
Some reviews only allow ICP management in the Metaview web app; an update against one is rejected. The review can also reject the ICP on its content; the error says why and what to do.
</instructions>

<response_format>{"application_review_id", "submitted_version_base", "status": "approved_and_ranking", "next"}</response_format>

<usecase>
Update a screen's candidate outreach — the invitation email and its schedule. Before any candidates are invited, it is simply saved and used once they are.

IMPORTANT: once candidates are invited this is not a draft. The change applies on the spot, with no separate confirmation or approval step, and applies to every outreach email not yet sent — including pending invitations and reminders of already-admitted candidates. The one thing that never moves is a deadline a candidate was already told: deadlines are snapshotted at admission.

This is a partial update — only the fields you pass change. Reminders use fixed system copy derived from the deadline. Outreach changes never re-score or re-interview anyone.
</usecase>

<instructions>
Always call get_screen_details first to read the current outreach and the active version number to pass as base_version (null when the screen has no active_version).
Subject and body may use template variables, substituted per candidate at send time: {{First name}}, {{Job title}}, {{Company}}, {{Interview length}}, {{Deadline}}, {{Days to deadline}}.
Not editable here: the sender mailbox, the email logo, and the ATS rejection reason used at the deadline — configured in the Metaview web app and preserved as-is.
Once candidates are invited, there must be no pending web-app edits (this change would apply those too).
</instructions>

sections.description: The complete, final interview plan as a list of section objects — the same shape get_screen_details returns in interview_plan.sections. FULL REPLACE: this replaces the current plan wholesale, and sections/questions not in the list are deleted — never send a diff or partial edit. Each section: {section_id, title, goal?, questions}. Each question: {question_id, prompt, kind?, options?, follow_up?, rubric?, output_type?, multi_select?, candidate_role?, character?}. kind is exactly one of 'conversational' (asked out loud), 'multiple_choice' (options required; options and multi_select apply only to this kind — multi_select true lets the candidate pick several options), 'slack_thread' (answered in writing), or 'role_play' (a spoken scene the interviewer plays in character; candidate_role is who the candidate is in the scene and character is the interviewer's private brief for who they play — both apply only to this kind). output_type is 'FIT', 'BOOLEAN', 'NUMBER', 'SHORT_TEXT', or 'DATE'. Keep the ids of nodes you carry over — kind, output_type, multi_select, and question history follow the id, and omitted fields are preserved from the current node; invent new unique ids for new nodes (defaults: conversational, FIT). Omit this parameter entirely to keep the current sections and update only the context fields (once candidates are invited, a context-only update still makes a new version).

description.text:
<usecase>
Replace a screen's interview plan. Before any candidates are invited, it is simply saved and they get it once invited.

IMPORTANT: once candidates are invited this is not a draft or a suggestion. The plan you pass takes effect on the spot as the next version — new interviews run against it immediately, with no separate confirmation or approval step. Only call it with a complete, final plan you are ready to put in front of candidates.

An update does NOT re-interview anyone. It does re-score: when the edit changes scoring content (a question's prompt, rubric, kind or options, its section's goal or title, or the role context — company context does not re-score), completed interviews nobody has decided on yet return to EVALUATING and are re-scored against the new plan. Candidates already progressed, rejected, or opted out keep their scorecard.

This update supersedes pending web-app PLAN edits. Pending CONFIG edits (outreach, language, welcome content) would reach candidates alongside it, so the update is rejected until they are applied with Update screen or reverted in the web app.
</usecase>

<instructions>Always call get_screen_details first: read the current plan, compose the full revised plan from it, and pass the active version number as base_version (null when the screen has no active_version). To roll back, read an earlier version's plan with plan_version=N there and submit its content back through this tool.</instructions>

<response_format>{"screen_id", "status": "updated"|"saved"|"no_changes", "version"?, "previous_version"?, "interviews_rescoring"?, "next"}</response_format>
